facts.note: Read the tag ref and pinned/tagged source files without chain or RPC access. This is the OS dependency listed by the existing Lido AST evidence.

The slots are keccak256(aragonOS.appStorage.kernel) and keccak256(aragonOS.appStorage.appId), read by kernel()/appId() and written by internal setters. Both select the implementation-resolution path and must be guarded rather than treated as unrelated Aragon state.

getAppBase is defined in contracts/apps/AppProxyBase.sol at the same pin. It reads the app's Kernel pointer and asks that Kernel for the implementation in the base namespace. Changing either the Kernel pointer or the app id changes the lookup.

facts.value: apps is mapping(bytes32 => mapping(bytes32 => address)) at regular slot 0; a selected member is keccak256(appId || keccak256(namespace || uint256(0))).
facts.note: KernelStorage declares apps first, then recoveryVaultAppId. KernelProxy inherits KernelStorage before helper bases; its implementation resolves the core member. Kernel inherits IKernel (interface), KernelStorage, and helper bases; getApp reads apps and _setApp updates the selected member after contract validation, emitting SetApp. The map uses exact storage keys and does not rely on event presence or preimages for these known members.

The same member is initialized by the KernelProxy constructor. Watching the stETH app-base entry without this member or the Kernel implementation's code would miss an implementation-resolution upgrade.
base and core are hashed as raw UTF-8 labels. The kernel core app id is the source's literal apmNamehash(kernel), not keccak256(kernel). Tests check the exact named-slot and namespace hashes.
Values come from aragon-kernel.proxy/implementation and app:lido.aragonApp/implementation. They are deployment-file declarations, not current chain observations or activation-block qualification.
